env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local
env CGO_ENABLED=0

# Vendor ownership comes from modules.txt, including unimported packages.
cd vendored
! logos list .
stderr '\[correctness::mixed_module\] module example.com/dep has Go packages \(example.com/dep/g\) and loGo/s packages \(example.com/dep/l\)'

# A nested module path is a separate owner in the flattened vendor tree.
rm vendor/example.com/dep/l/l.lgo
logos list .
stdout '^example.com/client$'
logos list example.com/dep/child
stdout '^example.com/dep/child$'
go list .
stdout '^example.com/client$'

# Workspace modules with overlapping import prefixes remain separate.
cd ../workspace
logos list example.com/shared/g
stdout '^example.com/shared/g$'
logos list example.com/shared/l
stdout '^example.com/shared/l$'

-- vendored/go.mod --
module example.com/client

go 1.27

require (
    example.com/dep v1.0.0
    example.com/dep/child v1.0.0
)
-- vendored/client.go --
package client

import "example.com/dep/g"

const Value = g.Value
-- vendored/vendor/modules.txt --
# example.com/dep v1.0.0
## explicit; go 1.27
example.com/dep/g
example.com/dep/l
# example.com/dep/child v1.0.0
## explicit; go 1.27
example.com/dep/child
-- vendored/vendor/example.com/dep/g/g.go --
package g

const Value = 1
-- vendored/vendor/example.com/dep/l/l.lgo --
package l
-- vendored/vendor/example.com/dep/child/p.lgo --
package child
-- workspace/go.work --
go 1.27

use (
    ./g
    ./l
)
-- workspace/g/go.mod --
module example.com/shared

go 1.27
-- workspace/g/g/g.go --
package g
-- workspace/l/go.mod --
module example.com/shared/l

go 1.27
-- workspace/l/l.lgo --
package l
